title: task edit create/edit flag split: extend the redirect + help to --assignee, --dependency and --modified-file (QCLI-283 follow-up)
description: QCLI-283 (DEC-172 (4ak) and (4aq)) fixed the create/edit flag-name divergence for --label and --reference: quest task edit now exits 2 naming the edit-side flags, the split is named in the help, NO alias is added, and no new manifest field carries it. Three more create-side spellings still fall through to the generic "Unrecognized flag" refusal with no edit-side redirect: create --assignee vs edit --add-assignee/--remove-assignee; create --dependency vs edit --add-dependency/--remove-dependency; create --modified-file vs edit --add-modified-file/--remove-modified-file. Apply the SAME shape: a real exit-2 refusal naming the correct edit-side flags, no alias, help names the split, and help-only with NO manifest field (DEC-172 (4aq)). Also narrow the QCLI-283 EDIT_FLAG_REDIRECTS docblock and help wording, whose "each"/"such as" claim overstates the map until these three are covered (QCLI-283 round-1 review, finding 1). Filed by the quest-cli worker at team-lead instruction.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each of quest task edit --assignee, --dependency and --modified-file fails at exit 2 naming the correct edit-side flag(s) to use instead (--add-assignee/--remove-assignee; --add-dependency/--remove-dependency; --add-modified-file/--remove-modified-file), with no alias and nothing written, tested via real exit-2 repros.
The task edit help text names the create/edit split for these three fields, and the manifest carries no new field for it (help-only, DEC-172 (4aq)).

The EDIT_FLAG_REDIRECTS docblock in src/cli/main.ts and the task edit help text name EXACTLY the flags the redirect map holds, so the each/such-as claim is true for every create-only spelling the map covers.

quest task edit --label x --badflag y exits 2 naming BOTH the create-only flag edit-side spelling AND every other unrecognized flag, as usageFailure did before opum-ai/quest-cli#574; exit code and atomicity (nothing written) are unchanged, and a test covers it.
bun run check exits 0 including the new coverage.

finalSummary:
Five criteria, the QCLI-283 flag-redirect family extended.

AC1: --assignee, --dependency and --modified-file join --label and --reference in EDIT_FLAG_REDIRECTS. Each now fails at exit 2 with a real repro naming the edit-side flags to use instead (--add-assignee/--remove-assignee, --add-dependency/--remove-dependency, --add-modified-file/--remove-modified-file), writes nothing (atomicity asserted by reading the record back), and is still NOT accepted as an alias -- the three are absent from task edit's allowed flags, and the exit-2 refusal is the proof.

AC4: a create-only spelling no longer HIDES another unrecognized flag. createSpellingFailure now takes the allowed list and appends the "Unrecognized flag(s)" sentence beside its redirect sentences, so `task edit --label x --badflag y` names BOTH in one refusal -- restoring what usageFailure gave before opum-ai/quest-cli#574 narrowed it -- with the exit code and atomicity unchanged. Proved BOTH WAYS: with the old message shape the new test goes red at its --badflag assertion, and green on the fix.

AC2/AC3: the task edit help names the whole split -- the five create-only spellings and all eleven edit-side flags -- and both it and the EDIT_FLAG_REDIRECTS docblock are held to the map's own key set, read from the source rather than restated, so a key added or dropped there moves the test. Help-only, per DEC-172 (4aq): no new manifest field.

AC5: bun run check exits 0 on the declared bun 1.4.2 -- 1166 CLI tests and the mod suite 45 pass / 0 fail.

A CHANGELOG entry records the user-visible half.
